title: The Secret Reason Horses Let Us Ride Them
beats: Fluffy sheep as bred artifacts; defines domestication as sculpting animals for human use; callback to Part 1
Few animals domesticated: why? Proposes building a checklist
Feedable: cow turns grass into steak, tiger turns steak into tiger; 10:1 energy loss rules out carnivores
Want unpicky herbivores eating what humans cannot
Friendly: carnivores, grizzlies, buffalo, hippos, giraffes all dangerous; war bears joke
Big and not dangerous means nervous: jogging down a gazelle that then leaps the pen
Fecund: pandas as the counterexample; need animals eager to breed
Must grow up fast; refines domestication vs taming
Aside: plants are domesticated too; pop-tart jab at going back to nature
Pig generations shorter than human ones vs elephant reproduction timeline
Elephants can be tamed not domesticated; rule of thumb farm=domesticated, circus=tame
Family: horses changed history; why not ride zebras out of Africa?
Zebras kick, bite, duck lassos; horse herd hierarchy lets humans become head horse
Same family logic for barnyard animals, chickens, dogs vs cats
Zebras lack society; look like horses outside, not inside
Checklist recap: Friendly, Feedable, Fecund, Family; must pass all, hence a baker's dozen

metrics.misconception: yes: zebras are basically horses (3:53, 4:51); also natural plants (2:26)
metrics.examples: ~15 animals, each a pass/fail case against one criterion; pairs (cow/tiger, pig/elephant, horse/zebra, dog/cat)
metrics.ending: Alliterative 4-F checklist recap explaining why only ~13 big animals were domesticated

principles.1: confirmed: fluffy sheep, cows, dogs and cats as home anchors 0:00, 4:31

principles.4: confirmed: cow as grass-to-steak machine (0:21) then thermodynamic ratio
principles.5: partly: gazelle chase and pen escape narrated literally 1:35
principles.7: partly: repeated pass/fail across animals lets the 'must pass all' rule feel obvious before 5:11
principles.9: confirmed: every criterion tested on several animals
principles.10: partly: criteria accumulate; examples do not grow in size
principles.11: confirmed: notes feedable before catching is 'pig before the pen' 0:48 and orders criteria
principles.13: confirmed: simple language plus a causal reason (thermodynamics, generation time) per criterion

new_moves.name: new:contrast-pair
new_moves.what: Teach each criterion via a near-twin pair where one passes and one fails

new_moves.name: new:mnemonic-label
new_moves.what: Alliterative names for criteria so the rule list is memorable

new_moves.name: new:rule-of-thumb-compression
new_moves.what: Collapse a subtle distinction into a one-line heuristic

theory: The video teaches a classification rule by stacking near-twin contrast pairs, each isolating exactly one criterion. Because the pairs share everything except the tested trait, the learner sees the cause; the alliterative checklist is then the compression of examples they've already judged.
velocity: Scene builder: a checklist panel that ticks/crosses per example, filling a grid of animals x criteria
Orchestrator: for classification topics, pick contrast pairs that differ in only the criterion being taught
Voice: offer a one-line rule of thumb after a subtle distinction (farm vs circus)
Learner model: probe misconceptions of surface similarity (zebra looks like horse) before revealing the hidden trait
Evals: flag lessons whose criteria lack at least one passing and one failing example
quote: a tiger a machine that turns steaks into… tiger
